means: The printed page rather than the screen - a comic as it appears on paper: panel borders, screentone dots in place of flat colour, speech bubbles, and no colour at all.
does: Brings the whole printed-page package, not just a line style. Expect greyscale, halftone screentone, and often panel borders or a gutter intruding into the frame. This is danbooru GRAMMAR: on the corpus 'manga' is a page-format attribute, so it drags panelling and monochrome in with it whether you asked or not, and it will silently kill every colour tag in the prompt. Treat it as a decision about what KIND of image this is, not as a flavour on top of one.
reach_for_it: for a deliberate page-as-image beat - a flashback rendered as a comic, a title card, an eyecatch - never as the general style of a colour film
used_in: no current film house style; adjacent to shot.fx.screentone, whose card review warns that 'monochrome' inside a screentone clause greyscales the entire frame
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
